business.description: Yuken India Limited is a leading manufacturer of high-precision, technology-heavy hydraulic systems and components in India, supported by friendly and intelligent technical support service. The company draws its engineering lineage from Yuken Kogyo Company Limited, Japan, a globally respected hydraulic equipment manufacturer of more than 95 years.

outlook.statement: The Company will approach the coming year with optimism moderated by caution. India's infrastructure, manufacturing and industrial development will continue to provide a favourable long-term demand environment, and the Company's optimism will remain anchored in India's long-term direction rather than its performance in any single quarter or financial year.

Revenue growth in the year ahead will be supported by India's industrial and infrastructure investments, new product introductions and the Company's broader geographic mandate, while margins recovery will depend on pricing discipline, productivity improvement, cost control and a higher capacity utilisation.

The Company maintained stable revenue growth during FY 2025-26 despite a challenging business environment. While profitability was impacted by higher operating costs, increased employee expenses and depreciation charges arising from investments in capacity and infrastructure, the strengthening of reserves and net worth reflects the Company's continued focus on long-term growth, operational resilience and value creation for stakeholders.

Yuken India will strengthen its domestic and international presence, deepen its solution capabilities and progress towards its aspiration of becoming a Rs 1,000 crore company. It will continue to combine innovation, powerful performance and reliability as it prepares for the next five decades.

Yuken India Limited is expected to operate in an environment of gradual but uneven industrial recovery, supported by sustained domestic capital expenditure and continued focus on manufacturing-led growth in India. The outlook for the hydraulics and fluid power industry remains stable with moderate growth potential, driven by infrastructure development, expansion in core sectors such as steel, power, railways, and defence, and increasing automation across manufacturing processes. The ongoing "China+1" supply chain realignment is also expected to create additional opportunities for domestic players in engineering and precision components. Demand for standard hydraulic products and aftermarket services is likely to remain steady, supported by a growing installed base and recurring maintenance requirements. The systems and project-based segment is expected to improve gradually, in line with revival in capital-intensive projects and improved execution cycles. However, the operating environment may continue to be influenced by global uncertainties, input cost fluctuations, and competitive pressures, which could impact margins and order visibility in the short term.

Cyclical Demand Risk: The business is dependent on core sectors such as steel, construction, machine tools, and infrastructure, which are cyclical in nature. Any slowdown in capital investment or industrial activity may impact demand for hydraulic products and systems.

Global Economic and Trade Risks: Ongoing geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions, and supply chain realignments continue to create uncertainty in global markets, potentially affecting export opportunities and input availability.
Input Cost Volatility: Fluctuations in prices of steel, castings, and other raw materials can impact cost structures and put pressure on margins if not fully passed on to customers.

Intense Competition: The industry is characterised by competition from both domestic and international players, leading to pricing pressures and the need for continuous product innovation and efficiency improvement.

Technological Evolution: Increasing adoption of alternative technologies such as electro-mechanical systems and advanced automation solutions may gradually influence demand patterns in traditional hydraulic applications.

Execution and Project Risk: A portion of revenues is derived from project-based systems, which are subject to delays in execution, extended approval cycles, and variability in customer spending timelines.
Regulatory and Compliance Risk: Changes in industrial, environmental, or safety regulations may require continuous adaptation in product design and manufacturing processes.
The Company is not exposed to any significant commodity price risks and has not undertaken any commodity hedging activities during the financial year.

The company's talent management strategy is focused on building a skilled, motivated, and performance-driven workforce, aligned with its long-term business objectives.
Emphasis is placed on continuous learning, capability development, and fostering a culture of innovation and operational excellence.
The company provides regular training and development programmes to enhance technical and functional competencies, along with structured career development opportunities.
Employee well-being is supported through a comprehensive benefits framework and initiatives aimed at improving engagement and retention.
Safety continues to remain a key priority, with well-defined protocols and practices implemented across all operational locations to ensure a safe and secure working environment.

As of March 31, 2026, the company's workforce comprises 794 employees across key functional areas including engineering, operations, management, administration, and trainees, supported by contract workforce as required for operational needs.

The newspaper advertisement published in the principal vernacular newspaper relating to dispatch of Notice of Postal ballot notice dated May 28, 2025 was in English language whereas the provisions of sub rule 3 of Rule 22 of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014 inter alia says that 'Advertisement shall be published atleast once in a vernacular newspaper in the principal vernacular language of the district in which the registered office of the Company situated'.

The notice of the Annual General Meeting was approved by the Board of Directors at its meeting held on May 28, 2025. Subsequently, an addendum to the said Notice was approved by way of resolution passed by circulation September 01, 2025. However, the AGM held on September 10, 2025 and the said addendum to the Notice was dispatched to the members without providing the clear twenty-one days' notice as per Section 101 of the Companies Act, 2013.

Pursuant to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/DIL2/CIR/P/2019/94 dated August 19, 2019, the Company was required to file the trading approval application with the Stock Exchange(s) within 7 working days from the date of receipt of listing approval from the Stock Exchange(s). The listing approval in relation to the preferential allotment was received on September 22, 2025; however, the Company filed the trading approval application on October 13, 2025, resulting in a delay of 7 working days. Consequently, NSE Limited levied a fine of Rs. 1,40,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Forty Thousand only), excluding applicable taxes, which was duly remitted by the Company on October 15, 2025.
